reasoning: Two independent models (qwen3-235b and deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD and found it to be standard AppImage packaging with pinned SHA-256 checksums from the official upstream GitHub repository. No malicious code execution, unexpected network requests, or data exfiltration mechanisms were identified. The chmod 4755 on chrome-sandbox is a known requirement for Chromium/Electron applications. The inconclusive verdicts were caused by tool errors (HTTP 400 API failure on .SRCINFO, parsing error), not security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused entirely by tool errors, not security analysis. Report 1 (qwen) failed to audit .SRCINFO due to an HTTP 400 error. Report 3 (openrouter/free, advisory only) failed to parse the model's response. Report 2 (deepseek) successfully audited both files and found them safe. The actual security-relevant content (PKGBUILD) was consistently deemed safe by all models that successfully analyzed it.
coverage_issues: Report 1: .SRCINFO audit failed due to HTTP 400 API error
Report 3: PKGBUILD audit failed due to parsing error; source_fetch not attempted
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parsing errors) should not block a security verdict when the security-critical files (PKGBUILD) have been successfully audited
.SRCINFO is metadata-only and doesn't contain executable code - a failure to audit it should not prevent a verdict if PKGBUILD is clean
The audit tool should distinguish between 'file unavailable due to tool error' and 'file has security concerns' when computing final verdicts
Advisory reports with tool errors should be clearly marked as non-voting to avoid confusion in disagreement analysis
